searchText: EIP-1153 was itself an alternative to EIP-2200 which ended up "winning" but I think EIP-1153 brings more advantages than just being an alternative, and I suppose that is why it is being looked at again now <@552133098075193354> I know it usually takes a day or two to make the notes from ACD. Is there anywhere else I can catch up on it in brief? The twitter threads are really great as summary. Maybe that’s enough for you until the notes are ready? https://twitter.com/timbeiko/status/1479481915325440008?s=21 <@364112345682804736> that was absolutely perfect. Thank you. And thank you <@552133098075193354> Sorry Im not good with Twitter When is Shanghai in general targeted for release? Couple months after merge? Six months after? TBD? Every month or so, I also share longer-form updates at https://hackmd.io/@timbeiko/acd/ TBD - the merge isn’t even scheduled yet + it’s still unclear what the scope of Shanghai will be Thanks again <@552133098075193354> really appreciate your notes after these calls. Helps to keep in the loop so much and dispel more complex conversations Is the thinking for the merge still that the spec has to be frozen by February in order to not exceed a June bomb diffusion? Or is that not really true There is probably some wiggle room, but that seems realistic. If you freeze in Feb, have clients in March, testnets in April, mainnet in May, roughly. None of these are exact, and if we found an issue at any stage we’d probably delay. It’s hard to predict, though, just because of unknown unknowns: best we can do is implement/test/break/fix things with as efficient of a cycle as possible 😄 🤞 I'm hoping this schedule is not followed. When I hear things like having clients in March (two months from now) I get a cold sweat having some staked ETH. With this timeline there's less than a couple months to test on something that looks close enough to mainnet. In my mind not having another fork to postpone the bomb is suicidal
